name: Angkor Wat (The City Temple)
description: The largest religious structure in world history, representing Mount Meru with five lotus towers surrounded by a massive 190-meter-wide moat.
history: Built as the state temple and royal funerary monument for Suryavarman II, gradually transitioning into a Buddhist pilgrimage site.
construction: Constructed from an estimated 5 million tonnes of sandstone quarried from Mount Kulen and floated down canals on balsa rafts.
architecture: Features concentric galleried enclosures, over 3,000 carved celestial Apsara dancers, and a continuous 800-meter outer wall of mythological bas-reliefs.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1992 and national symbol of Cambodia.
currentStatus: Standing and preserved in Siem Reap, Cambodia.
